newsitem.title: ITALY: Soccer-British firm buys Vicenza soccer club.
newsitem.headline: Soccer-British firm buys Vicenza soccer club.

text.p: Serie A soccer club Vicenza was sold by auction to a British investment company, Stellican, in an Italian bankruptcy court on Friday, court officials said.

Stellican's succesful lone bid, of 22.75 billion lire ($13.5 million), made Vicenza the first foreign-owned club in Italy. Two other bidders, both Italian, dropped out of the race and only Stellican representatives were in court.
Vicenza, who were promoted to serie A in 1995, have qualified for next season's European Cup Winners' Cup.
Based in the affluent northeast city of Vicenza, the club has a profitable balance sheet but was put into receivership as a result of bankruptcy affecting the owners.
Stellican, closely linked to U.S. investment group Apollo, specialises in buying distressed companies, according to British media reports.

Managing director Stephen Julius told the London Financial Times on Wednesday that his group wanted to redevelop the ageing Romeo Menti stadium, invest in new players and develop sponsorship and merchandising. But he added that he was worried that a foreign takeover would prove unpopular with local fans.
